answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake and earn a place in a shared atlas of verified work history before it can transact at full limits. A newcomer starts capped, and each honest completed job adds a verifiable entry, so trust spreads like a ripple outward only from proven behaviour. A fake identity is cheap to create but expensive to age: an attacker must fund and maintain a separate stake and history for each plume of sock-puppets, while misbehaviour forfeits the bond and erases that history.
